questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, then select the option "No error".**

And, indeed, there was hardly picture in Rome I was unable to reattribute to its rightful owner.

options.text: to reattribute to its rightful owner.
hardly picture in Rome I was unable

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 4'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The segment in the sentence that contains a grammatical error is* "hardly picture in Rome I was unable".*
 
• The** error lies in **the missing article before "picture".
 
• In English, **countable singular nouns usually **need an article or other kind of determiner like 'a', 'an', or 'the'.
 
• Article** 'A'** will be used before word** 'Picture'** as it is starting with a consonant.

Therefore, The **correct sentence** is: *"And, indeed, there was hardly **a picture** in Rome I was unable to reattribute to its rightful owner."*

questions.question:
Choose the option that is the correct indirect form of the sentence.

She said, "I will be available tomorrow."

options.text: She said that she would be available tomorrow.
She said that she would be available the next day.
She said that she must be available the next day.
She said that she will be available the next day.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'She said that she would be available the next day'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **correct indirect form** of the sentence *"She said, 'I will be available tomorrow.'*" is *"She said that she would be available the next day."*
 
• **When changing direct speech into indirect speech, t**he verb tense typically shifts back (this is known as "backshifting").
 
• In this case, **"will" **becomes "**would".**
 
• Moreover, words indicating nearness in time or place in direct speech are generally changed into words showing distance in indirect speech.
 
• Here, **"tomorrow" **changes to** "the next day".**

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: '*She said that she would be available the next day.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1, "She said that she would be available tomorrow,"** is incorrect because "tomorrow" should be changed to "the next day" in indirect speech.
 
• **Option 3, "She said that she must be available the next day,**" is incorrect because "will" should not change to "must" in indirect speech. "Must" changes the meaning, implying a necessity or obligation that wasn't present in the original sentence.
 
• **Option 4, "She said that she will be available the next day,"** is incorrect because the verb "will" should be backshifted to "would" in indirect speech.

questions.question:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.

Our study goes

P. beyond LDL cholesterol levels to get

Q. and the impact of eating walnuts daily

R. a complete picture of all of the lipoproteins

S. on their potential to improve cardiovascular risk
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 3' **i.e. **'PRQS'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The correct order for the sentence is** PRQS.** Here's why:
 
• **"Our study goes"** is the** starting clause **and should be followed by something that elaborates on what the study aims to do or achieve.
 
• **P.** "beyond LDL cholesterol levels to get" - This **segment indicates that the study is aiming **to achieve something more than just understanding LDL cholesterol levels.
 
• **R. **"a complete picture of all of the lipoproteins" - This** clause elaborates** further on what the study is trying to achieve, making it clear that it's not just about LDL cholesterol, but a complete understanding of all lipoproteins.
 
• **Q.** "and the impact of eating walnuts daily" - This **adds another dimension **to the study. After getting a complete picture of all the lipoproteins, the study is also considering the impact of a specific diet factor - eating walnuts daily.
 
• **S.** "on their potential to improve cardiovascular risk" - **Finally, this clause ties everything together **by explaining the ultimate aim of the study, which is to understand how all of these factors could potentially improve cardiovascular risk.

Therefore, the** rearranged sentence** is: *"Our study goes beyond LDL cholesterol levels to get a complete picture of all of the lipoproteins and the impact of eating walnuts daily on their potential to improve cardiovascular risk." Hence, the correct answer is** PRQS.***

questions.question:
Choose the option that is the correct passive form of the sentence.

We had eaten the cake.

options.text: The cake had been eaten by us.
The cake will be eaten by us.
The cake is eaten by us.
The cake was eaten by us.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **When we convert** a sentence from active to passive voice, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• The **passive form** of **"had eaten" is "had been eaten".**
 
• Thus, the active sentence "We had eaten the cake"** changes to** "The cake had been eaten by us" in the passive voice.

Therefore, the **correct answer **is: '***The cake had been eaten by us.'***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's look at the other options:
 
 
• **"The cake will be eaten by us." **- This is the future simple passive form, not the past perfect (which is the tense of the original sentence).
 
• **"The cake is eaten by us." **- This is the present simple passive form, not the past perfect.
 
• **"The cake was eaten by us."** - This is the past simple passive form, not the past perfect.

questions.question:
Some parts of a few sentences have been jumbled up, and labelled A, B, C and D. Select the option that gives the correct sequence in which these parts can be rearranged to form a meaningful and grammatically correct sentence.

I didn't speak to the sage again for many years,

A. seer, born on a dark island of a union between an ascetic and a fisher princess

B. because of the many hefty books, he'd written. Vyasa the

C. though I heard of him from time to time. I learned

D. his name: Vyasa the Compendious,
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 3'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The** correct sequence** to form a meaningful and grammatically correct sentence is **CDBA.**
 
• Let's break it down:
 
 
• **C.** "though I heard of him from time to time. I learned" - **This segment forms the continuation** of the first part of the sentence ("I didn't speak to the sage again for many years") as it explains what happened during the years of not speaking to the sage. It also creates a logical link to the next segment (D) by mentioning that the speaker learned something.
 
• **D. **"his name: Vyasa the Compendious," - **This segment provides the information** the speaker learned, i.e., the sage's name. It also logically leads to the next segment (B) which adds more information about Vyasa.
 
• **B. **"because of the many hefty books, he'd written. Vyasa the" - **This segment adds additional information **about Vyasa, and then ends with a partial phrase ("Vyasa the") that logically leads to the final segment (A), which completes this description.
 
• **A.** "seer, born on a dark island of a union between an ascetic and a fisher princess" - **This segment finalizes the description** of Vyasa, completing the sentence in a coherent and meaningful way.
 
 

Therefore, the** correct sentence **is: *"I didn't speak to the sage again for many years, though I heard of him from time to time. I learned his name: Vyasa the Compendious, because of the many hefty books, he'd written. Vyasa the seer, born on a dark island of a union between an ascetic and a fisher princess." So, the correct answer is CDBA.*
